Without timeoutMs a quick command behaves as before. runMutate: build a repo whose source has a loop that a mutation turns endless (e.g. `while (i < n) { ...; i++ }` style code where flipping a comparison makes the test hang - make sure at least one produced mutant really hangs by using a tiny file whose only mutation points are in that loop, and check the output rather than assuming which one), call runMutate with timeoutMs 2000: it returns (does not hang), prints at least one `[KILLED]` line ending in `[timeout]`, the summary line has the `(<n> by timeout)` form with the right n, the source file is byte-identical to the original afterwards, and the return code is 0 when every mutant is killed. A repo without any hanging mutant prints the old summary line with no parenthesis. Capture console output by temporarily replacing console.log / console.error. Give each node:test a generous timeout option (60s) because every hanging mutant costs the timeout.
